item.title: tiny-secp256k1: Stale buffer after ignored wasm failure accepts invalid infinity tweak
item.description: Summary The three-argument xOnlyPointAddTweakCheck path ignores the wasm failure return and compares an unchanged input buffer. When the tweak result is the point at infinity, this stale-buffer comparison can return true for an invalid derivation. Details xOnlyPointAddTweakCheck in index.ts has two code paths. The path taken when the caller omits tweakParity discards the return value of the wasm call and compares…

item.title: fzf: Predictable FIFO path in zsh completion allows local symlink attack / arbitrary file overwrite as the victim user ( fzf feed fifo)
item.description: Summary shell/completion.zsh feeds every trigger-driven zsh completion through a FIFO at a predictable, PID-based path in shared /tmp ( fzf-complete-fifo-$$ ), without checking the failure of rm -f / mkfifo . On a multi-user host, another local user can pre-create that path as a symlink to a victim-writable file (e.g. ~/.bashrc ), causing the victim's own completion to overwrite it with the completion stream — with…

item.title: fzf: Arbitrary command execution via bash arithmetic expansion on unvalidated layout size in fzf-tmux (-l/-u attached value)
item.description: Summary bin/fzf-tmux fails to validate layout size values given in the attached form (e.g. -l50 ). For -l / -u these values reach bash arithmetic expansion ( $(( max - size )) ), where an operand like a $(cmd) executes cmd as the invoking user during option parsing — before any tmux interaction and even outside tmux. A second sink embeds unvalidated popup geometry ( -x/-y/-w/-h/-p ) into an unquoted tmux popup ...…

item.title: Next.js: SVG rejection bypass in the image optimization
item.description: On self-hosted deployments, the Next.js image optimizer ( / next/image ) can be made to process an attacker-supplied SVG even when SVG support is disabled with dangerouslyAllowSVG: false (the default). This reaches an SVG parser the application intended to keep disabled, increasing exposure to denial of service and SVG decoder vulnerabilities.

item.title: Next.js: HttpOnly cookie exposure through internal response header on Next.js Edge runtime routes
item.description: Next.js applications that set cookies through NextResponse on Edge runtime routes — App Router route handlers and Pages Router Edge API routes — send an internal x-middleware-set-cookie header in the public response, duplicating the cookie value and its attributes. This makes HttpOnly cookies, such as session tokens, readable by JavaScript running on the same origin when an application sets a sensitive cookie on an…

item.title: Next.js: Cross-client response injection and disclosure in self-hosted Next.js applications forwarding fetched responses
item.description: Self-hosted Next.js applications (App Router route handlers and the fetch cache) that return a fetched upstream response unchanged can emit a response whose declared framing does not match the body actually sent. When such an application sits behind an HTTP/1.1 reverse proxy that permits pipelined response queueing, a crafted upstream response can desynchronize responses between clients, enabling response injection…

item.title: Next.js: Cross-user cache disclosure and poisoning in Next.js use cache with binary arguments
item.description: Next.js App Router applications that pass binary arguments (such as Uint8Array or Blob values) to functions using the use cache directive can produce identical cache keys for distinct arguments, allowing cached results to be shared across users — cross-user disclosure of cached data or cache poisoning. This affects applications using use cache with binary arguments.

item.description: Self-hosted Next.js applications served with next start and built with cacheComponents: true but without Partial Prefetching accept a request-supplied route param value as a prerender placeholder. One unauthenticated GET request can poison the fallback shell cache entry that a family of routes shares. Such a route is served from a shell that keeps its never-prerenderable params as placeholders, so every value of…

item.title: Safari MCP: JavaScript injection through single-quoted tool arguments (backslash not escaped)

An argument containing a backslash followed by a quote therefore closed the literal, and the rest of the argument ran as JavaScript in the page. Seven of the affected arguments belong to read-only tools that are exempt from the tab-ownership…
